safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated contains no family history statement.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting a statement about noncontributory family history has minimal impact in an acute assessment of an insect sting reaction and does not change immediate management. It may slightly reduce documentation completeness but is unlikely to affect clinical decisions here.

safety_verdicts.content: There is no evidence of cellulitis.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting that there is no evidence of cellulitis could lead to some ambiguity about whether a secondary skin infection was considered, potentially prompting unnecessary follow-up or antibiotics. However, in this context (acute sting with localized rash/swelling), it is unlikely to materially change care if the rest of the assessment is documented.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting advice to ring back for reassurance/concerns (especially given anxiety about breathing) could reduce access to timely re-triage if symptoms evolve or anxiety escalates. While alternative safety-netting (e.g., go to A&E if worsening) may exist, loss of this follow-up option can modestly increase risk of delayed support.

safety_verdicts.content: No known drug allergies; no food or pet allergies.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Contradicts gold and transcript: patient is allergic to penicillin, so 'NKDA' is incorrect (food/pet allergy negatives are not sufficient to negate penicillin allergy).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Incorrectly documenting 'no known drug allergies' when the patient reports a penicillin allergy can directly lead to inadvertent prescribing/administration of penicillin-class antibiotics. This creates risk of serious allergic reaction, including anaphylaxis, which can be life-threatening.

safety_verdicts.content: No known drug allergies; no food or pet allergies.
